# Incident Report — Vidar Stealer Infection
**Evidence source:** `2022-01-07-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,880 packets, 750.8 sec capture) + exported HTTP objects
**Analyst:** Network forensics review, tshark-based

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **192.168.1.216** |
| MAC address | **9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** (confirmed via DHCP option 12, NBNS, and Kerberos machine account `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2$`) |
| Logged-in domain user | **steve.smith** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString `steve.smith`) |
| Domain / DC | `spoonwatch.net`, DC = SPOONWATCH-DC (192.168.1.2) |

## Malware family

**Vidar Stealer** — attribution is **signature-confirmed**, not just behavioral, based on the exact C2 protocol structure observed on the wire:

1. HTTP checkin over TCP stream 65 to `2.56.57.108:80` (no DNS lookup preceded it — hardcoded IP C2), using the well-known Vidar/Arkei-family WinHTTP fingerprint:
   `Accept: text/html, application/xml;q=0.9, ... image/jpeg ... image/x-xbitmap, */*;q=0.1` / `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8` / `Accept-Charset: iso-8859-1, utf-8, utf-16, *;q=0.1`
2. Sequential `POST /osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg` — server responds with `Content-Type: image/jpeg` but the payloads are actually **PE DLLs disguised as .jpg**. Extracted strings confirm legitimate NSS/CRT support DLLs Vidar downloads to parse Firefox/Chromium credential stores: `freebl3.dll`, `VCRUNTIME140.dll`, `CONCRT140.dll`, plus SQLite/NSS library strings (`nssckbi.dll`, `NSS 3.36.4`, `secmod.db`) inside the payloads.
3. `POST /osk//main.php` — final C2 checkin/config confirmation (empty body response, HTTP 200).
4. `POST /osk/` — exfiltration upload, multipart form field `name="file"; filename="_5861695120.zip"` (379,629 bytes), matching Vidar's characteristic `_<digits>.zip` naming convention.

The exfil archive (`osk`, SHA256 below) unzips to the canonical Vidar log-folder layout, which removes any ambiguity:
```
autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt
autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt
cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt          (credit card grabber)
cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt
cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt
cookies/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt
outlook.txt
passwords.txt
screenshot.jpg
system.txt
```
This layout (autofill/cc/cookies/passwords/system/screenshot buckets, uploaded as a single zip after downloading browser-decryption DLLs) is Vidar Stealer's signature exfiltration behavior, not shared by other stealer families' folder conventions (RedLine, Raccoon, Mars use different naming).

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` (TCP, HTTP, no DNS resolution used — hardcoded IP)

**Malicious URLs (all on the single C2 session, tcp.stream 65, starting at t=202.87s)**
- `hxxp://2.56.57.108/osk//6.jpg`
- `hxxp://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg`
- `hxxp://2.56.57.108/osk//2.jpg`

- `hxxp://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php`
- `hxxp://2.56.57.108/osk/` (exfil upload)

**Malicious domains:** none — the C2 was contacted by raw IP with no A/AAAA lookup in the DNS traffic, consistent with Vidar's hardcoded-IP configuration.

## Notes

- No email, exploit-kit, or drive-by delivery vector is present in this capture — the trace begins with normal AD/Kerberos logon and Windows/Microsoft telemetry traffic; Vidar is already resident and beacons to C2 starting at t=202.87s, so the initial infection vector predates this capture.
- The `am_delta_patch_*.exe` and Windows Update `.cab` files pulled from `download.windowsupdate.com` / `au.download.windowsupdate.com` (23.38.189.201/225) and `ctldl.windowsupdate.com` (8.253.189.126) are legitimate Microsoft Defender definition updates — not part of the malware chain — confirmed by hostname, user-agent (`Windows-Update-Agent`, `Microsoft-Delivery-Optimization`), and Microsoft-owned IP ranges.
- All other external TLS destinations (52.168.112.67, 20.50.80.210, 204.79.197.200/203, 52.183.220.149, 20.189.173.1, 40.83.240.146, 104.212.67.47) resolve via SNI to legitimate Microsoft/Bing telemetry and update services and are not implicated.
